images.caption: Figure 2:Overview of MT Forcing.(a) Single-Turn DMD matches student rollout marginals to single-turn teacher distributions. (b) Teacher-Forcing Guidance supervises history-dependent transitions on reference trajectories via flow matching to encourage cross-turn consistency. (c) Overall training: teacher-forcing warmup followed by DMD with teacher-forcing regularization.
Figure 3:Visual quality across turns with a single-turn teacher.Each bundled prompt is applied independently to the source image. Enlarged crops show stable facial details.
Figure 3:Visual quality across turns with a single-turn teacher.Each bundled prompt is applied independently to the source image. Enlarged crops show stable facial details.
Figure 4:Content inconsistency of the single-turn teacher.The teapot’s floral pattern changes across independent edits with bundled prompts, as highlighted in the enlarged crops.

Figure 5:Qualitative results on the step-wise sub-bench.SenseNova-U1 and SenseNova-U1.5 are compared before (left) and after (right) MT Forcing at Turns 1, 4, and 8. MT Forcing reduces artifacts while preserving accumulated edits.

Figure 6:Qualitative ablation of MT Forcing.SenseNova-U1.5 is compared with Single-Turn DMD only, Teacher-Forcing Guidance only, and the full method at Turns 4 and 8. Enlarged crops highlight differences in texture detail.

Figure 7:Visual quality comparison under different regularization weights.From left to right: the source image and outputs withλTF=1,0.5,0.25,0.1\lambda_{\mathrm{TF}}=1,0.5,0.25,0.1. Enlarged crops show differences in fur detail.
